title: Generic Result, Option, and API wrapper patterns
hook: Result<T, E> and Option<T> model success/failure and presence/absence as generic wrappers — they replace thrown exceptions in typed pipelines and mirror Rust/C# railway-oriented patterns without runtime overhead.

blocks.text: **Result<T, E>** is a discriminated union: `{ ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. **Option<T>** (or `T | null` with helpers) models optional values explicitly. Generic wrappers centralize error handling — `map`, `flatMap`, `unwrap` methods parameterized on `T` and `E`. TypeScript has no built-in Result — teams define their own or use `neverthrow`, `fp-ts`. At runtime these are plain objects; generics guide compile-time flow. C# has `Result<T>` in modern libraries and `Nullable<T>` for value types.

entries.plainDefinition: Success value T or error E — never both.
Some T or None — explicit optional without null confusion.
Chain operations on Result — errors short-circuit the track.
Extract T from Ok or throw on Err — boundary between typed and exception style.

blocks.text: API layers that return `Result` force callers to handle errors — no forgotten try/catch. `fetch` wrappers return `Result<ResponseBody, NetworkError>`. Parsing JSON returns `Result<T, ParseError>`. Reddit senior threads debate Result vs exceptions — TypeScript lacks checked exceptions, so Result types document failure modes in the signature. C# `OneOf` and Rust `Result` inspire TS patterns; TS adds discriminated union narrowing on `.ok`.

blocks.title: Result vs throw
blocks.body: Result for expected failures (404, validation). Throw for programmer bugs and unrecoverable states.

blocks.body: Overusing Result for internal code — exceptions fine for invariant violations.

blocks.title: Forgetting to check ok
blocks.body: Accessing .value without narrowing — use if (r.ok) or switch.

blocks.text: Libraries: `neverthrow` provides `ResultAsync` for Promise chains. `fp-ts` `Either<E, A>` is the FP variant. Combine with Zod: `safeParse` returns `{ success, data, error }` — same shape as Result. Generic `E` should be a discriminated union of error kinds for exhaustive handling. Performance: Result objects allocate — negligible vs network; avoid in hot inner loops.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot implement Result map/andThen. Mixing throw inside Result. No discriminant for narrowing.

interviewTakeaways: Result<T,E> = discriminated union Ok | Err — errors in type signature.
map transforms value; andThen chains Result steps; Err short-circuits.
Option models presence — alternative to null with explicit None.
60s: Generic wrappers encode success/failure without exceptions. Discriminant ok enables narrowing. Use at API boundaries. TS has no built-in Result — union + helpers.
Follow-up: neverthrow, Zod safeParse, exhaustive error unions.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "Result is a runtime class" — plain object union.
Strong: "Discriminated Result union. map/andThen chain. Narrow on ok. Err for expected failures."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS uses exceptions for all failures — Result pattern adds typed error channels TS can narrow.
C# Result and Rust Result are first-class; TS implements via generic discriminated unions with zero runtime wrapper.
